s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of a painless swelling over a pacemaker site with persistent systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Painless swelling over the pacemaker site
Persistent fatigue, dyspnea, and cough after COVID-19 infection
Soft tissue mass with increased vascularity surrounding the device on chest ultrasound
CT imaging confirmed soft-tissue mass around the pacemaker pocket
key_facts: 70-year-old man with history of nicotine use
Remote history of laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma
Remote history of bladder urothelial carcinoma
Dual-chamber pacemaker implantation for sick sinus syndrome 9 months prior
Postoperative checks showed normal pacemaker function
Clinically unremarkable pocket at postoperative checks
Tested positive for COVID-19 infection three weeks before presentation
Fatigue, dyspnea, and cough persisted and worsened after COVID-19 infection
New swelling over the pacemaker site reported at routine cardiology visit
Normal blood pressure and heart rate on examination
No signs of cardiac decompensation or cachexia
Chest ultrasound revealed soft tissue mass with increased vascularity
CT imaging excluded haematoma or infection

shortlist.label: Pacemaker pocket sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: New swelling over pacemaker site with soft tissue mass and increased vascularity on imaging

shortlist.label: Metastatic laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma and new swelling at pacemaker site

shortlist.label: Metastatic bladder urothelial carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of bladder urothelial carcinoma and new swelling at pacemaker site

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Soft tissue mass with increased vascularity on imaging, consistent with aggressive vascular tumor

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Persistent systemic symptoms and new swelling at pacemaker site, with lymphoma a possible cause of such symptoms

raw.rationale: The presence of a soft tissue mass with increased vascularity surrounding the pacemaker site, as shown by chest ultrasound and CT imaging, along with the exclusion of haematoma or infection, supports this diagnosis. The history of pacemaker implantation and the development of a mass at the site of implantation also points towards this rare but recognized complication.

rejected.label: Metastatic laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: The remote history of laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (7 years prior) makes recurrence less likely, and the specific location of the mass around the pacemaker site suggests a local rather than metastatic process.

rejected.label: Metastatic bladder urothelial carcinoma
rejected.why: Similar to laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma, the remote history (10 years prior) and the localized nature of the mass around the pacemaker make metastasis from this primary site less likely.

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: While angiosarcoma could present as a soft tissue mass, the specific context of a pacemaker pocket and the exclusion of other diagnoses make Pacemaker pocket sarcoma a more direct explanation for the findings.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: Lymphoma could present with a wide range of symptoms and findings, but the localized nature of the mass around the pacemaker site and the absence of systemic symptoms or signs of lymphadenopathy make this diagnosis less likely in this context.
